clue.text: Cunning tramp, for example

definitions.meaning: a tramp steamer is one kind of vessel

explanation.definitionFit: Craft means guile, and also a boat, of which a tramp steamer is one sort.

clue.text: Duplicator should supply author's requirement

definitions.meaning: a copying machine ought to produce the copy correctly
the legal right protecting a writer's work from reproduction

explanation.definitionFit: Copyright is the legal protection a writer needs; read in two words it is a copy made correctly.

clue.text: Joint cooked by Ken — a pound

indicators.note: something cooked is altered or doctored, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A cut of meat roasted by Ken costs a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between foot and leg.

clue.text: Hill has adviser that's a pest

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a mentor is a trusted adviser

explanation.surface: A hill contains a counsellor who is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps harassing is a pest or nuisance.

clue.text: Welsh warrior gives scowl without result

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to scowl is to glower
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A Welsh fighter frowns but achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: GLOWER is wrapped around END.
explanation.definitionFit: Owain Glyndwr, anglicised in Shakespeare's Henry IV, led a Welsh revolt against English rule.

clue.text: Seized wild badger round its head

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece
something running wild is out of order, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: the head of the badger, its opening letter B

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed a wild badger by the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges BADGER as GRABED, and 'round' wraps it about B, the badger's head letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seized is to have been grabbed or snatched.

clue.text: Fire, for instance, or part of one

definitions.meaning: fire is one of the four classical ..., with earth, air and water
the heating coil in an electric fire

explanation.definitionFit: Fire was one of the ancient elements; an electric fire's heating coil is also called that.

clue.text: Dockers' leader had row took punch perhaps

indicators.note: the leader of the word Dockers' is its opening letter

parts.note: a rank is a row or line, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: A union boss of dock workers argued and threw a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' looks like a blow after a row, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Punch is a mixed drink, so someone who drank may have taken punch.

clue.text: Offender rode?

parts.note: the word rode is the letters of doer put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Was the criminal on horseback?
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer is someone who commits an offence.

clue.text: Painter put up estimates

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: in a down clue the word put is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to put is to set or place

explanation.surface: An artist hung up his price quotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rates are estimates or valuations, as in rating a property for local tax.

clue.text: Still features in the game?

parts.note: motionless facial features worn at the card table, where a bluff depends on giving nothing away

explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless look, named after the card game where hiding one's hand matters.

clue.text: In the vicinity of a fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing contest or fight

explanation.surface: Somewhere near a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: About as a preposition means near or around a place.

clue.text: A feminine style of ruff with feathers

definitions.text: A feminine style of ruff with feathers

parts.words: A feminine style of ruff with feathers
parts.note: reads like a frilly Elizabethan collar for women, but the ruff is the wading bird and its female is meant

explanation.definitionFit: The female of the ruff, a wading bird, has its own name, distinct from the male.

clue.text: Results of mishandling by bargee. Ask for repair

indicators.note: something sent for repair is to be fixed and reassembled, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A canal boatman damages goods and is told to get them mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for repair' rearranges the letters of BARGEE and ASK. A bargee is a British canal boatman.
explanation.definitionFit: Things broken through careless handling are breakages.

clue.text: Admitted Gaullist leader talked wildly

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of the word Gaullist

parts.note: to rant is to talk wildly

explanation.surface: A French Gaullist chief raved and later confessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitted, as in conceded, is a synonym of granted.

clue.text: Military body of red-caps, including King

parts.note: army is a military force

indicators.note: the police word takes the royal letter inside it

parts.note: Redcaps is the British nickname for the Royal Military Police, so they are cops
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The army's military police contain a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. Redcaps are British military police, named for their red caps.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps of several divisions is a large military body.

clue.text: Mark as dealt with by reprimand

definitions.meaning: to put a tick against an item on a list once it is done
to scold someone, a British colloquialism

explanation.definitionFit: Ticking off items on a list marks them done; a ticking-off is also a scolding.

clue.text: Girl is to study the driving position

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the stance is how a golfer stands to drive the ball

explanation.surface: A girl sets out to learn how to sit behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' suggests a car, but it is a golf drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a girl's given name.

clue.text: This journalist reveals general rising over the channel

indicators.note: France shows within it the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: France lies across the English Channel from Britain

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A reporter exposes a general climbing in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns LEE into EEL, which 'reveals' places inside FRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance writer works for many papers on commission rather than on staff.

clue.text: Sound quality \student found in the instrument

parts.note: timbre is the tone colour or quality of a sound
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A pupil discovers the tone of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan shows a stray mark before 'student'; it is a smudge, not a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbrel is an old tambourine-like percussion instrument from the Bible.

clue.text: Letting ale vary mixed gins

indicators.note: to vary the word is to change the order of its letters
the letters of the word gins are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub lets its beer vary and its gin cocktails mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vary' makes LEA from ALE; 'mixed' makes SING from GINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasing a property is letting it out for rent.

clue.text: A fashionable old actor, of course

parts.note: in means trendy or in fashion
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree, the Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A stylish veteran thespian, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but course is a racecourse. AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous racecourse near Liverpool.

clue.text: He hears of a checker

definitions.meaning: from Latin audire, to hear: a listener
an accountant who inspects financial records

explanation.definitionFit: Auditor literally means a listener, and also an inspector of accounts.

clue.text: Would it help to keep Jemima's feet dry?

definitions.text: Would it help to keep Jemima's feet dry?

parts.words: Would it help to keep Jemima's feet dry?
parts.note: Jemima Puddle-Duck of Beatrix Potter's tales is a duck, so a walkway for a duck is imagined

explanation.definitionFit: A slatted wooden walkway laid over mud keeps feet dry; Jemima is a duck.

clue.text: Decline and Fall — nothing in it

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the word for fall that precedes it

parts.note: to fall is to drop
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Gibbon's Decline and Fall turns out empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Gibbon's history 'The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire'.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or decline.

clue.text: Tack or otherwise treat the joint

definitions.meaning: to tack is to sew with long loose stitches
to spoon fat over roasting meat

explanation.definitionFit: Basting is loose temporary stitching, and also moistening a roast with its juices.

clue.text: The foreign child's backward with this sum

indicators.note: the whole string formed by the foreign article and the child is to be read from the end

parts.note: la is French for the
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A foreign child does sums badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns LATOT around in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the sum reached by adding figures.

clue.text: Object that is approved?

parts.note: an object, but also what is accepted as proper, as in the done or in phrase

explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object, and the thing is what is fashionable or acceptable.

clue.text: Manful monsters?

parts.note: read man-full: monsters full of men, having eaten them

explanation.definitionFit: Giants of fairy tales are known for eating people, so they end up full of men.

clue.text: Camping by one on purpose

parts.note: someone camping is sleeping in a tent
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Going camping alone deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on purpose' looks like one phrase, but 'on' supplies letters and 'purpose' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is an aim or purpose.

clue.text: No bid by Green?. Could be he's taken for a ride

parts.note: in bridge, pass is the call that makes no bid

indicators.note: suggests the letters of green might be something else rearranged

explanation.surface: A bridge player called Green passes, then gets fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges GREEN into ENGER. 'taken for a ride' sounds like being conned, but just means carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller carried in a vehicle he is not driving is literally taken for a ride.

clue.text: Old ten-dollar bird

definitions.meaning: a former United States gold coin worth ten dollars

explanation.definitionFit: The US once minted a ten-dollar gold coin by that name, also a large raptor.
